title: The Adversarial Path to the Personal Assistant: Sumit Agarwal
talk_summary: A consumer personal-assistant product talk (Ario) focused on adversarial ETL of user data and personalized RAG, with a short but concrete engineering section on when not to use an LLM. The transferable content is the 'avoid the LLM at all costs' principle, edge-first data abstraction, and right-data-at-right-time context discipline.

takeaways.what_they_do: They compute derived values (e.g., run duration) with plain code/columns instead of asking the model, reserving the LLM only for genuinely non-deterministic work.
takeaways.evidence_quote: use the llm last try five ways try seven ways try nine ways of doing something before you resort to the llm

takeaways.technique: Abstract raw data into profiles before the model sees it
takeaways.what_they_do: Raw source data (DoorDash, Amazon) is distilled into compact profile objects; the LLM reasons over refined summaries and only drills into raw data when needed.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we try to give processed and refined data to the llm as an input so that it can figure out how to strategize properly

takeaways.technique: Answer near the edge; avoid pulling raw data
takeaways.what_they_do: They structure retrieval so as many questions as possible are answered from refined layers close to the model, going back to raw data only as a fallback.
takeaways.evidence_quote: The more questions you can answer closer to the edge of the system closer to the llm without having to go all the way back to your raw data the better off you'll be

takeaways.technique: Deliberately withhold data from pipeline stages
takeaways.what_they_do: They spend effort NOT putting too much data into each pipeline stage because overloaded stages become complicated and degrade.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we spent a lot of energy in trying to actually avoid putting too much data into various parts of the pipeline

takeaways.technique: General hints instead of prescriptive instructions
takeaways.what_they_do: Rather than hardcoding 'subtract column 17 from column 4', they give a general nudge ('try manipulating the columns') and let the model find the relation.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we wouldn't say subtract column 17 from column 4 that's very prescriptive we would give it a general instruction
